stem: A read-heavy service uses a Redis cache in front of PostgreSQL. Which caching strategy avoids the classic "cache-stampede" problem after a key expires?

options.text: Setting a much longer TTL and never invalidating

explanation: Adding a per-key mutex (a.k.a. single-flight / request coalescing) ensures only one caller repopulates the cache while the others wait, preventing thundering-herd hits on the database.

optionExplanations.B: Doesn't help — writes may still coincide with a cache miss.
optionExplanations.C: Defeats the purpose of a cache.
optionExplanations.D: Trades staleness for a different (worse) failure mode.

stem: Which statements about the CAP theorem are **true**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: During a network partition, a distributed system must choose between availability and consistency.
A CP system can still serve reads if a partition happens, as long as they hit the primary partition.
An AP system continues to serve requests during a partition at the cost of possible staleness.
CAP guarantees you can pick two of {C, A, P} in all circumstances, including no partition.

explanation: CAP is a partition-time trade-off; when the network is healthy you can have both consistency and availability. The choice between C and A only becomes binding under a partition. Option D misrepresents the theorem as an unconditional pick-two.

optionExplanations.B: Correct — CP degrades availability in the minority partition, but the majority can continue.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong — it's a partition-conditional trade-off, not an unconditional one.

distractorRationales.D: The common oversimplification of CAP as an unconditional 'pick two'.

sourceRefs.title: You Can't Sacrifice Partition Tolerance (Coda Hale)

stem: You need exactly-once **processing** across a producer, a broker (Kafka), and a consumer. Which combination is required in practice?

options.text: Best-effort broker with no ordering guarantees
A single consumer thread per topic partition, always

explanation: "Exactly-once processing" is achieved by making the consumer idempotent (or transactional) on top of at-least-once delivery; strictly-exactly-once end-to-end delivery over a network is a stronger property that requires coordinated writes.

optionExplanations.D: A performance choice, not a semantics guarantee.

stem: (Draft / not yet reviewed) SLO of 99.9% availability over 30 days allows how many minutes of downtime?

optionExplanations.C: That would be closer to 98.8% SLO.
optionExplanations.D: Close, but arithmetic is 43.2 → A is more precise.
